Definition: feminine accusative case singular of G3117 (G3598 being implied); at a distance (literally or figuratively):--(a-)far (off), good (great) way off.
BiblicalUsage: Makran means far off, a great way off, and it measures the distance between a sinner and home. Luke 15:20 has the prodigal yet a great way off when his father saw him and ran, and Mark 12:34 has Jesus telling the scribe, thou art not far from the kingdom of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two distances here are the whole gospel: a great way off, and not far, and the Father running the gap between them.
